html:
Qusayr 'Amra is a small bath house and hall in the desert east of Amman, built in the early 700s for an Umayyad prince, probably the future caliph al-Walid II. It is one of the Umayyad desert castles.

Its walls and ceilings are covered with paintings: hunting scenes, musicians, dancers, bathing women, the six kings defeated by the Umayyads, and a dome painted with the stars of the zodiac, one of the oldest known pictures of the sky on a dome.

The paintings show that early Islamic rulers kept many of the tastes of the Roman and Persian courts. The building became a World Heritage Site in 1985. See also the Umayyad Mosque in Damascus and Jordan.
